messages.author: f4491d27aeb3d644
messages.subject: rw1 random effect error
parts:
Background:
I am predicting the winner of a basketball game and I want to account for the traveling distance in my model. For the home team, it is 0, however, for the away team, it varies(0~3/4000). 
If I treat it as a fixed effect, the feature has no effect(all 0 for mean, 0.025,0.5,0.975 quantile). If I treat it as a random effect with "rw1", error occurs:
Error in inla.check.location(location[[r]], term = gp$random.spec[[r]]$term,  :
  Locations are too close for f(travel, model="rw1", ...):  min(diff(sort(x)))/diff(range(x)) = 9.014e-07 < 1e-05
  You can fix this by some kind of binning, see ?inla.group
  If you want/need to bypass this check at your own risk, do
    > m = get("inla.models", inla.get.inlaEnv())
    > m$latent$rw1$min.diff = NULL
    > assign("inla.models", m, inla.get.inlaEnv())
Would you please give me some hints? I have tried to scale the feature, and it didn't work.
Thank you !!

messages.author: ef76f4ec1ca10943
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] rw1 random effect error
parts:
You may want to use the function inla.group()  to group your distances.

I hope that helps 
Iosu
